Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Customer exploring Dedicated vs Hosted for low-latency payment-fraud inference; primary concerns are noisy neighbor isolation, 99th percentile SLAs, and on-prem/VPC KMS integration.
- Redwood to run targeted benchmarks (95/99 pctl) using customer's anonymized trace; follow-up on KV cache behavior and batching profiles.

Transcript (timestamps approx every 30s, transcription imperfect):
[00:00:05] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a deep dive into serving topology and isolation patterns — today Marco's going to walk through benchmarks and then we can dig into your traffic shape. 
[00:00:20] Lina: Hi all, sorry for the slight delay, joining from SF office. We're mainly worried about 99th pctl latency, we saw big tail spikes on our current hosted vendor during peak batch settlement windows.
[00:00:30] Marco: Cool, can you give us the rough RPS and average token lengths? That helps when we model batching.
[00:00:38] Raj: Our 95th latency target is <120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and 99th ideally <300ms, during nightly reconciliation we can spike to ~1k RPS for a 10min window.
[00:00:49] Marco: OK, that's a useful target. Important nuance — continuous batching helps throughput but increases tail if you let batching windows grow; Redwood supports latency-first policies which cap batch delay to maintain SLOs.
[00:01:05] Tomás: Are those caps configurable per-route? We have a mix of interactive and batch endpoints.
[00:01:12] Marco: Yes per-route and per-model version. You can set max batch size, max wait ms, and a QoS priority. We also do prefix KV caching which can remove the prefix tokens from compute for repeated patterns.
[00:01:26] Aisha: Quick sec — from security perspective we need to know about key management. If we go Private we need a KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for encryption at rest and in transit.
[00:01:36] Jillian: That's supported; Private deployments can connect to customer KMS, and we capture audit trails. We'll share the integration matrix after this.
[00:01:46] [00:02:05] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[00:02:30] Marco: I'm going to share my screen, the microbench summary — caveat these were run on Cuda v12 stack and our optimized kernels.
[00:02:40] [00:03:00] Marco (screen): Slide: "Dedicated vs Multi-tenant: latency and tail behavior". We ran three configs: Hosted multi-tenant (best-effort), Hosted tiered (reserved slices), and Dedicated GPU pool. For your trace we expect Dedicated to reduce 99p by ~40-60%.
[00:03:18] Lina: Is that for exact same model and quantization?
[00:03:21] Marco: Yes same 7B model, int8 quantization for all runs, note quantization lowers token-latency but can increase memory pressure if kernel path not optimized — oh and sometimes the transcript tool calls it "quanization" haha.
[00:03:36] Raj: Can you explain the difference between "reserved slices" and Dedicated? We haven't used those terms in our infra.
[00:03:43] Marco: Sure — reserved slices are like soft-partitions inside a shared pool, you get priority scheduling and guaranteed minimum throughput but still share hardware. Dedicated is physical isolation: your tenants get pinned GPU instances with no cross-tenant scheduler interference.
[00:03:58] [00:04:20] Tomás: How do you handle preemption or evictions in reserved slices?
[00:04:26] Jillian: There's a multi-tier scheduler: you can choose strict isolation (no preempt) or preemptible slots that give cost efficiency. For preemptible we maintain graceful drain with KV cache persistence and checkpointing so warm caches are restored quickly.
[00:04:44] Aisha: When you say KV cache persistence, is the cache encrypted and can it be stored in our VPC?
[00:04:51] Marco: Yes, for Private deployments KV cache can be stored on customer-managed VPC storage, encrypted with your KMS. For Hosted, cache is kept in Redwood-managed memstores but we provide encryption at rest and access logs; we'll detail separation controls.
[00:05:05] Priya: Quick aside — noisy neighbor in multi-tenant shows up either as GPU saturation or host-side network spikes; we've seen cases where a single tenant's large beam search-ish job creates garbage collection effects that affect co-tenants.
[00:05:19] Lina: That's the problem we saw last month with another provider — sudden job caused 99th to triple. How do you detect and mitigate in real-time?
[00:05:27] Marco: We do per-tenant telemetry and can apply automated throttles and fallback routing to lower-cost model variants. For Dedicated you avoid that entirely, but there are tradeoffs in capacity commitment.
[00:05:39] [00:05:55] Raj: What about burst windows — we can't commit to peak monthly all the time, so burst capacity is needed. Dedicated plus burst sounds expensive.
[00:06:03] Marco: We offer hybrid patterns: Dedicated baseline with shared burst pools, and you can configure automatic fallbacks to hosted-compatible variants if your dedicated pool is saturated. Cost is controlled by policies (e.g., block bursts over X mins).
[00:06:16] Tomás: Can we set SLOs that auto-scale Dedicated as long as we keep a cap? Like scale to N GPUs but stop at M to control cost?
[00:06:24] Jillian: Yes autoscaling policies can enforce max/min GPU counts and scaling cooldowns. But remember scaling takes time — for sudden 10x spikes we recommend a blend of dedicated baseline and burst on shared pool.
[00:06:36] [00:06:55] Marco: Now the KV cache numbers: with a 45% hit rate we saw ~30% reduction in tail latency for repeated prefix workloads. But warmup matters — cold start hit-rate is low, so warm caches are important for real SLOs.
[00:07:10] Lina: Our prompts are often templated — that should help hit-rate right?
[00:07:15] Marco: Exactly, templated prompts are perfect for prefix caching. Also Redwood has automatic prefix normalization to increase hit-rate across minor variations. Note the transcriber sometimes writes "K-V cash" or "K V cash" in the raw logs.
[00:07:28] Aisha: For on-prem what are the OS/kernel hints? We run RHEL and need guidance on NIC tuning and IRQ balancing.
[00:07:35] Jillian: We'll produce an ops checklist: NIC settings, hugepages, GPU driver pinned versions, and cgroup configs for device isolation. We'll attach that.
[00:07:46] [00:08:15] Marco: Quantization caveat — int8 gives significant perf and memory wins, but re-quantized kernels can slightly change latency variance. For critical low-latency SLOs, we recommend a tuned int8 path validated on your sequence length distribution; we'll bench both int8 and fp16 for your prompts.
[00:08:32] Tomás: Any chance quantization impacts output fidelity? We have sensitive risk models, can't tolerate regressions.
[00:08:38] Marco: We'll run evals on your golden prompts, Redwood Optimize ties quantization recommendations to quality regression alerts so you can gate deploys.
[00:08:46] [00:09:05] Raj: Back to noisy neighbor — do you provide per-tenant QoS throttles at request ingress so we can protect critical routes?
[00:09:12] Marco: Yes per-route quotas, RBAC, and token-level cost attribution. You can set higher priority for fraud-detection route and lower for analytics.
[00:09:22] Lina: What's the troubleshooting workflow if we see tail increase? Alerting -> run perf profile -> rollback?
[00:09:28] Jillian: Our console has tracing hooks, per-token time breakdown, and you can do live thread dumps for the runtime. Typical flow: alert -> automatic canary rollback to previous model version -> SE-run perf capture -> remediate.
[00:09:42] [00:10:10] Speaker 2: um hmm
[00:10:30] Marco: I want to show a heatmap: 99th latency across 24h in multi-tenant vs dedicated. Notice the multi-tenant has periodic spikes aligned to other customers' scheduled jobs. Dedicated is flat.
[00:10:45] Raj: Does Dedicated still cause noisy-host issues at the hypervisor layer?
[00:10:50] Marco: With Dedicated we pin GPUs and isolate the hosts; hypervisor-level noisy neighbor is minimal — we also use network QoS and EBS throughput reservations for storage-backed caches.
[00:11:03] Aisha: Does Redwood certify or provide attestation for physical host separation in Dedicated? We need something for our SOC 2 vendor inventory.
[00:11:10] Priya: Yes we can provide architectural attestation and a runbook for compliance. For Private on-prem we provide more granular evidence since you control the fabric.
[00:11:21] [00:11:45] Tomás: On the scheduler, are there hooks to prioritize certain request ids? We sometimes tag high-value transactions.
[00:11:52] Marco: You can pass priority headers and Redwood will honor them in routing and batching priority — it's used in our scheduler to preempt lower-priority batches.
[00:12:05] Raj: Curious about cold-start behavior with caches after deploys — how fast can you warm?
[00:12:12] Marco: We have a few strategies: proactive pre-warm using replayed traces, background warmers that run at low priority, and persistent KV stores across container restarts for Dedicated pools. Warmup time depends on hit-rate and the size of the cache; we'll simulate with your trace.
[00:12:26] Aisha: Anything special for PCI-sensitive data flows?
[00:12:30] Jillian: We avoid storing PCI in logs; for Private you can configure token scrubbing at the edge and bring-your-own-key. We'll include the strictest controls in the compliance doc.
[00:12:40] [00:12:55] Marco: Now a quick demo — synthetic run of 1k RPS 128-token workload, comparing 99th pctl: hosted multi-tenant 99p = ~420ms, hosted reserved 99p = ~290ms, Dedicated 99p = ~160ms (numbers approximate, depends on quantization and seq len). 
[00:13:20] Lina: That's promising. Are the Dedicated numbers with caching enabled?
[00:13:24] Marco: The Dedicated benchmark had warm KV cache with ~60% hit-rate. If you disable caching the numbers shift.
[00:13:31] Raj: How do we measure that in our environment? We need the raw histograms.
[00:13:35] Marco: We'll share p99/p95 histograms and raw logs from the run — that's one of the next steps.
[00:13:44] [00:14:05] Speaker 3: (crosstalk)
[00:14:25] Tomás: For on-prem Private, what's the minimum rack-level footprint? We have limited datacenter space.
[00:14:32] Jillian: Minimum is usually 1-2 GPU hosts for an initial cluster, depends on model family. For 7B with int8, you can run on a couple of A100-ish machines; we'll size based on your workloads.
[00:14:45] Lina: We also have regulatory constraint to keep data in EU; how does Redwood Hosted handle data residency?
[00:14:51] Priya: We have region controls for Hosted; for EU-only workflows we can route requests to EU regions, and for strict residency we recommend Private deployment in EU.
[00:15:02] Aisha: We need proof that cached data never leaves region — is that logged?
[00:15:08] Marco: Logging includes region and host meta; we'll produce an example log schema.
[00:15:20] [00:15:40] Raj: Pricing question — what is cost delta between reserved slices and Dedicated?
[00:15:46] Priya: Reserved is cheaper upfront but doesn't fully eliminate tail risk. Dedicated has a fixed monthly commit that buys isolation. We'll send a delta sheet with a few scenario examples.
[00:15:58] Marco: Also factor in unit token cost — caching and batching reduce per-token compute and can make Dedicated more economical at scale.
[00:16:10] [00:16:30] Tomás: Do you support pinned kernel versions? We have strict change windows.
[00:16:35] Jillian: For Dedicated and Private yes, we can pin runtime images and certify driver versions. Hosted has a rolling upgrade model but we announce maintenance windows and provide compat notes.
[00:16:45] Aisha: Regarding audit logs — retention windows and export formats?
[00:16:51] Priya: Enterprise plans include extended retention; logs can be exported to your SIEM or S3 with encryption.
[00:17:05] [00:17:25] Marco: Okay, I'm going to walk through an edge case: long sequences with kvcache. If you have many long sequences, KV cache size can grow and evictions cause variance in latency. Dedicated helps because you control cache storage size and eviction policies.
[00:17:40] Lina: How do you size KV store? Is it in RAM only?
[00:17:44] Marco: It can be in-memory or backed by fast NVMe. For Dedicated you can reserve larger NVMe with throughput guarantees. For Hosted we manage it but provide memstore quotas.
[00:17:56] Raj: Is there an observable metric for cache pressure? Something we can alert on?
[00:18:00] Marco: Yes hit-rate, eviction-rate, and cache latency histograms; alerts can be configured on eviction-rate spike.
[00:18:10] [00:18:35] Tomás: If we use burst into hosted, can we force fallback models to a cheaper architecture during overflow automatically?
[00:18:42] Marco: Yes you can set fallback policies per-route: e.g., if Dedicated pool is saturated, route to a quantized-compatible hosted variant with graceful degradation.
[00:18:55] Aisha: Does fallback change tokenization or model output format? That could break downstream parsers.
[00:19:00] Marco: We ensure same API surface and structured outputs; we also recommend a smoke test set to validate parity. Redwood Optimize can run those smoke tests automatically on rollouts.
[00:19:12] [00:19:35] Priya: Quick poll — Lina, would you lean Dedicated given the numbers?
[00:19:39] Lina: We're leaning that way for core fraud routes but want hybrid for billing/analytics.
[00:19:46] Raj: Need to check budget but prefer predictable p99.
[00:19:50] [00:20:10] Marco: For the bench we'll need your anonymized trace and prompt examples. Also tell us which routes are latency-critical vs cost-tolerant.
[00:20:18] Tomás: We'll provide traces and a list of golden prompts by Friday.
[00:20:24] Aisha: And I'll provide security scoping items.
[00:20:30] [00:20:48] Marco: One more technical note — kernel selection at runtime: the serving engine chooses different kernels based on seq len and batch shape; sometimes int8 kernel is slower for very short sequences because of packing overhead. We'll model that for you.
[00:21:05] Lina: Interesting, so there is no one-size-fits-all quantization.
[00:21:09] Marco: Right, it's workload dependent.
[00:21:30] [00:21:55] Speaker 4: uh-huh
[00:22:10] Marco: Next, tracing: we emit per-request token time breakdowns and you can correlate with your traces (trace id header). That helps isolate whether slowdowns are compute, network, or batching delays.
[00:22:29] Raj: Can we ingest those traces into our NewRelic?
[00:22:33] Priya: Yes we support major APMs and also have a Prometheus endpoint for metrics.
[00:22:45] Aisha: Any known single points of failure in Dedicated?
[00:22:50] Jillian: For Dedicated you run control-plane redundancy and isolate data-plane; we recommend multi-AZ placement. For on-prem we recommend at least N+1 GPU hosts for high availability.
[00:23:05] [00:23:25] Marco: OK final part — example remediation playbook: detect spike -> identify tenant -> apply temporary throttle or route to fallback -> capture perf trace -> if persistent, spin up more capacity or engage SE for kernel tuning. We'll provide a templated runbook.
[00:23:41] Lina: That runbook will help; please include SLAs for our legal review.
[00:23:48] Priya: Will do — we'll include example SLA language and uptime/latency targets for Dedicated.
[00:24:05] [00:24:30] Raj: Anything about model pinning during rollouts? We want to avoid quality regressions.
[00:24:36] Marco: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic rollback on quality regressions; we tie evals to rollout gates.
[00:24:45] [00:25:05] Tomás: Are there RBAC controls for dev teams to deploy model variants?
[00:25:10] Priya: Yes role-level permissions; you can separate teams and require approvals.
[00:25:30] [00:25:50] Aisha: For Private/on-prem service mesh integration, do you support mTLS?
[00:25:55] Jillian: Yes mTLS, mutual auth and sidecar patterns are supported.
[00:26:10] Marco: Wrapping up bench plan: we'll run three experiments against your trace: (1) Hosted reserved baseline, (2) Dedicated baseline, (3) Dedicated with reduced quantization variance and warm pre-warm. We'll provide histograms and raw logs.
[00:26:30] Tomás: Great, thanks.
[00:26:40] [00:27:00] Priya: Final recap — Redwood to run bench and share results; Marco to upload KV cache microbench; Priya to send pricing; Aisha to send compliance items; customer to share traces and golden prompts.
[00:27:14] Lina: Thanks everyone, feel good about next steps.
[00:27:20] Raj: One last Q — do you have examples of customers in payments?
[00:27:24] Priya: We have references, we'll share a short case study and an intro if needed.
